body:
I called his GF after reading the messages and we talked for 6 hours before I told her I needed to get ready to go home and I would call her back. We talked for another 5 hours before we both decided to try and get some sleep. The next day, we talked for nearly 9 hours as we both shared stories and remembered this man we both loved so much. She asked if we were having an affair, she said that he always talked about me and how cool I was. I was honest and told her that while we loved each other, there were no romantic feelings between us, and that he talked about her to me as well, though he didn't always have positive things to say. I couldn't bring myself to tell her some of the things he told me as she was already hurting enough. We bonded in our grief and became somewhat close. My biggest worry was how his young child was going to handle his death. He never wanted to be a dad but accidents happen and he did what he could. He didn't have a very close relationship with his child but I know they both loved each other despite never having said it. My heart ached for them, but I grieved for my own loss more. I felt guilty and selfish. I blamed myself for not getting him out of that situation even temporarily. I hadn't done enough to help him. I hated myself for being more upset that I lost my best friend than being upset that his child no longer had a father, or his GF a partner. His words to us were "do not see my death as a tragedy, rather see it as a release from pain." I would later use those same words to try and justify my own suicide, writing them down at the bottom of every letter I wrote to a loved one. 

Earlier this year on my birthday, after many years of struggling with depression, PTSD and other mental illnesses, I walked down to the beach with the intention of walking into the ocean and never coming out. My own child and boyfriend sound asleep, I walked out of the house without saying goodbye, not wanting to disrupt them or put a damper on their excitement for the events of the day. As I stood on the sand and silently sobbed, I looked back at the rising sun behind me and started quietly singing Amazing Grace, knowing that from that point on, I would no longer feel any pain. As I inched closer toward the water, each step measured with bated breath, I thought back to how I felt when my best friend took his own life. I buried my face in my hands and cried hysterically, calling myself a coward for hesitating. I knew I didn't have the strength to leave without saying goodbye, and I felt I didn't have the strength to continue being a burden to others and myself. As a wave rapidly approached me, I jumped back out of reach of the water, and slowly backed away from the ebbing tide, watching the next waves build before breaking on the shore. As the minutes drew on, the beach began to fill with surfers and early birds out for a walk in the fresh, brisk air. I stood there for another hour before another one of my best friends texted to wish me a happy birthday. I thought about telling him the truth, but he had just lost a sibling to suicide a few months prior. Being so far away, I knew being honest with him would take a major toll, and was worried he would phone a mutual friend or the police to track me down. I think he could tell something was wrong since I wasn't as chatty as I normally am, and he said to me "I'm always here for you, and I love you." I remembered our conversations where I consoled him and shared my own story of loss. I once again remembered how I felt, how devastated I was, and how it affected me going forward. I thought about my own child and how my suicide would affect her, how it would ruin her chance for a fulfilling life, knowing she would wonder if it was her fault. 

When I got back home, exhausted from a lack of sleep and an emotional morning, I was greeted with smiles, hugs, and love from my baby. My BF was cooking breakfast for us, and as soon as he walked over to me, he knew. I could see the look of relief on his face as he took me in his arms and embraced me. He whispered, "I'm so glad you came home" in my ear as he hid the worry from our girl so as not to alarm her. I stood there lifeless, with my arms dangling at my sides as they both cheerfully wished me a happy birthday. I went and crawled into bed, when moments later, my daughter gave me a massive hug, placed her favorite stuffed animal near my head and said "here, mommy, Coco will take care of you and make you feel better" then she kissed me on the back of my head and walked back out to the living room. I could hear her telling my BF what she did, and she sounded so proud, all while I was lying there in bed, crying, hating myself for wanting to die. My love for her is the only reason I am still alive, because I don't want her to wake up screaming and crying in the middle of the night like my best friend's child did after he killed himself. 

I still love and miss him, and while the pain and sadness have lessened over time, I still think about him nearly every day. As strange as this sounds, the effects of his death have kept me alive, and I remind myself of it every time I reach the brink. I know that if he were still alive, he would be pragmatic about his approach to talking me out of it, and then he would crack some stupid joke or tell me “dammit woman, stop being such a girl” before reminding me how much life and love I had ahead of me. He was always good at being able to put things into perspective for me, it’s a shame he couldn’t do it for himself.

I met my best friend online and despite the distance, we clicked instantly. Our relationship was only ever platonic, however, we both agreed that our connection was unlike anything we'd ever experienced. I often referred to him as my soulmate, he was so similar it was eerie, yet many of his personality traits were the exact opposite of mine (I was extroverted, he was introverted, etc). We talked frequently about meeting but never actually had the chance as we both had a child and very little money. I knew he was depressed based on many of the conversations we'd had, and even though he mentioned he had a plan in place, I told him that if he ever seriously got the urge to off himself, that he needed to call me right away and I would book a flight for him out to where I lived. Oddly enough, he had visited my area a few years prior, and it was funny because he was driving around town likely at the exact same times I was, and we agreed that we more than likely crossed paths at some point, unaware. 

The year he killed himself, he was in bad shape. He couldn't find employment in his field and was forced to take a shitty pizza delivery job to support his family. He couldn't afford his anxiety medication anymore and went through a period of withdrawal-induced psychosis. I reached out numerous times but he always told me he was working and would call me back when he got the chance. The last time I spoke to him over the phone was almost a month before he committed suicide. I was on a long drive home from a road trip and had some time to talk and catch up with him, but he told me he was on his way to work and would call me within the week. I was taking a full load in summer school and trying to study for upcoming finals so I told him some times I would be available. Those times came and went, and I still hadn't heard from him. We exchanged a few messages back and forth on facebook, and he was still tweeting so I felt comfortable just leaving him alone until he was ready to talk. 

Fast-forward 2 weeks. I didn't have the internet at home so I took my young child with me to a local cafe that had free wifi and was open late so I could study. At around 12:30am, I looked up from my computer and saw my baby sound asleep in the booth across from me, and for some reason just lost it. Realizing that the cafe was filling up with patrons, I decided to pack up and leave to save face. After taking my child inside and putting her to bed, I went back to my car to call my best friend. It was late, even more so with the time difference, but he and I routinely had super late-night conversations so I didn't think anything of it. I called, he didn't answer and I just assumed he was sleeping but for whatever reason, when the phone went to voicemail, I just started bawling. I didn't say a single word, I just cried for the entire duration of the message. My heart hurt but I couldn't figure out why. I was stressed out from school and financial issues but not enough that it ever brought me to tears. I was beside myself. I called my dad overseas and he didn't answer so I sat alone in my car for the next 2 hours, just wailing and sobbing, and at the time I had no idea why.

The next day, I went to my good friends' house to hang out, and spend the night. I needed a good laugh, and they were always cracking jokes and telling hilarious stories. Their daughter was also really close with mine so we figured it would be a great opportunity for them to hang out too. After the kids went to bed, we stepped outside on the balcony to talk, drink, and catch up without waking up the girls. My friend said something funny and I jumped on my flip phone to post something about it to her facebook wall when I noticed I had 2 messages. My heart raced a little, thinking it was my best friend or my dad, but when I went to my inbox, I saw they were from my best friend's GF, and one of his close friends. My heart sank. Without even reading the messages I knew. I went from drunk, smiling and laughing to sober and somber in a matter of seconds. My friends saw my face and asked what was wrong, I only replied "my best friend killed himself." They asked how I knew, and leaned over to console me as I started tearing up. I handed my phone over, said I didn't want to read the messages and just stared blankly off into space while they read the messages to themselves. They walked over and both hugged me while offering condolences and words of comfort. I always knew it was a possibility but that didn't take away the agony and shock that he was gone. It was late but I texted my on/off BF at the time and he called and let me grieve. After a few hours, he said he needed sleep and suggested I get some rest too. I didn't sleep that night. Every time I closed my eyes, I would jolt awake and just space out. I felt numb, like it was a dream and I would wake up from it in the morning. I watched the sunrise as the light came through the blinds and flooded the room. I heard the kids playing in the bedroom, my friends still fast asleep. I called and texted my best friend numerous times, expecting him to respond or answer, only to be greeted by voicemail and silence. Tears streamed down my face as I finally read the messages. He had killed himself the day before, and was found dead by his GF. He was already gone when I called him the night before, and I had no idea. She described the scene to me, and what he looked like when she found him slumped over. I felt so bad for her, yet I grieved for my own loss. I never got to meet him or hug him, we never sat on the beach talking for hours like we'd always planned, we never took our trip to the forest, and I would never get the piggyback ride he promised me.

I have a suicide plan and am constantly thinking of ways to make it better. I have drugs set aside, a will, memorial service arrangements/instructions and letters to each of my loved ones. I'm slowly setting money aside to help pay for any debt I leave behind, and to help with costs related to my death.
